body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

Addressed the unbounded-retention finding in ed66ef0931fa19dd521fac433870c86a78687a30. A private storage allowance per capped BGP invocation charges actual indexed-slot, row-buffer, variable-buffer and owned-string capacities. Non-fitting scans use per-step scratch ownership; stale entries are dropped and refunded before replacement. This bounds newly retained storage, not total query heap or aggregate concurrent/nested invocations.

Actual independent Claude Opus 5 review approved this correction for CI and confirmed the retention bound. Ten focused tests pass in each of three configurations; compiled controls catch excessive retention, length-based undercounting and missing refunds. Root verified every generated allocation/timing sample against its raw output and executable hash.

Generated local diagnostic summary (macOS arm64, release O3, one Rayon worker):

```json
{
  "head": "ed66ef0931fa19dd521fac433870c86a78687a30",
  "main": "e53464c73f31f7aca800f3867ac054c36408e346",
  "cache_allowance_bytes_per_capped_BGP_invocation": 4194304,
  "allocation_samples": 24,
  "extra_peak_requested_bytes": {
    "five_patterns": 2240579,
    "eight_patterns": 2240867,
    "two_pattern_first_hit": 192,
    "two_pattern_full_miss": -2064243
  },
  "system_timing_samples": 40,
  "two_pattern_median_candidate_to_main": {
    "first_hit": 1.0206169079082827,
    "full_miss": 0.8552200575154927
  },
  "many_pattern_median_candidate_to_main": {
    "five_patterns": 0.9262564199712866,
    "eight_patterns": 0.9496322446244045
  }
}
```

The larger-pattern memory regression is bounded, with additional peak memory still present. All five paired timing repetitions improve in each larger-pattern case. I accept the bounded memory-for-latency tradeoff for these measured cases; the two-pattern first-hit cost remains disclosed. These local diagnostics do not establish universal neutrality or canonical speedups.

The original unbounded-retention finding is addressed. I also checked the suppressed uncached-RHS lifetime comment in the current-head Copilot review: `uncached` is declared inside the non-bind `else` at [exec.rs:4254](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/blob/ed66ef0931fa19dd521fac433870c86a78687a30/crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs#L4254). That branch ends at line 4290, before `record_pattern_ndv` at line 4291. Its owned `Bindings` therefore drops before NDV recording and before the remainder of the block. This ordering also covers armed-budget and non-fitting scans; an extra explicit drop is unnecessary. I decline that finding on the actual lexical scope, with no production change.

My source/memory review hold can now be cleared. Fresh protected CI is still running, so merge admission remains pending; no CI protection or performance floor has been changed.
